Find the Esri Wayback captures that image each feature

Source: R/dft_wayback_captures.R
dft_wayback_captures.Rd

For every feature of aoi and every Wayback release, reads the release's capture metadata and returns the capture (acquisition date, resolution, sensor) the release's tiles show there. A release date is not a capture date (see dft_wayback_releases()), so this is the table to choose imagery from: pass it to dft_wayback_pick() for the capture nearest a date, then fetch it with dft_wayback_fetch().

Usage

dft_wayback_captures(
  aoi,
  zoom = 17:19,
  releases = NULL,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  force = FALSE
)

Arguments

aoi

An sf, sfc or terra::SpatVector of POINT, POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON features, in any CRS.

zoom

Integer vector of tile zoom levels, each in 10 to 22 (default 17:19; zoom 17 is about 0.7 m on the ground at 54 degrees north). Zoom 10 stands for every zoom at or below 10. The metadata describes zoom 23 too, but GDAL cannot open the tile service there (the world is 2^31 pixels wide, one past its limit), so a capture at 23 could not be fetched.

releases

A release table from dft_wayback_releases(), possibly filtered, to search only some releases. When NULL, every release.

cache_dir

Character. Cache directory. When NULL, uses dft_cache_path().

force

Logical. Re-read the metadata even if cached (default FALSE).

Value

A tibble with one row per (feature, release, capture): feature (the row of aoi), release_id, release_date, capture_date (Date), res_m (the source's resolution in metres), source (provider and sensor, e.g. "Maxar WV02"), zoom and cover. Sorted by feature, release date and capture date. Zero rows, with a warning, when no capture covers any feature.

Details

Each release's metadata service has one layer per scale band, and layer L describes the tiles at zoom 23 - L. That mapping is handled here: pass the tile zoom levels you would fetch at. For each feature and release one zoom is kept, and the zoom column is the zoom to fetch at: the deepest zoom whose footprints cover the whole feature, since its tiles are the sharpest that leave no hole. Where no zoom covers a polygon whole, the zoom covering most of it is kept. For a point this is simply the deepest zoom that covers it.

Footprints overlap, and the tiles draw the one with the highest DrawOrder on top (then the finer source). Points and polygons are answered differently:

  • A point gets the one capture drawn on top at it. cover is 1.

  • A polygon can show several captures in one release. Every distinct capture visible over it is returned, with cover the share of the polygon's area where that capture is the one drawn on top. A capture wholly hidden under another earns no row, and the covers of one release sum to at most 1 (less where a base layer or no imagery shows). dft_wayback_pick() prefers the larger cover only among captures equally near the date, so filter on it first (for example cover >= 0.5) when a capture must image most of a patch. A fetch over a polygon is a mosaic of whatever its release shows there, not one capture.

A footprint with no capture date is a base layer, not a capture, and yields no row. A feature that no capture covers is absent from the result.

One metadata query is made per release and zoom over the bounding box of all of aoi (paged), not one per feature. Responses are cached under dft_cache_path(); a past release's metadata does not change, so only force = TRUE re-reads them. A new query bounding box (a grown or moved aoi) is a new cache entry.

See also

dft_wayback_pick(), dft_wayback_fetch().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aoi <- sf::st_read(system.file("extdata", "example_aoi.gpkg", package = "drift"))
pts <- sf::st_as_sf(sf::st_sample(aoi, 10, type = "regular"))

# Every capture over the points, in releases from 2017 on
rel <- dft_wayback_releases()
cap <- dft_wayback_captures(pts, releases = rel[rel$release_date >= "2017-01-01", ])
table(format(cap$capture_date, "%Y"))

# The capture nearest mid-July 2017 at each point
dft_wayback_pick(cap, as.Date("2017-07-01"))
} # }
